title: Tenali Rama and the Heavy Pumpkin
moral: True wisdom comes from knowledge, not wealth.

scenes.summary: The king gives a challenge to his courtiers.
scenes.text: One day, the king gave each courtier a pumpkin and asked them to fill it with the wisest thing.
scenes.image_prompt: king giving pumpkins to courtiers in royal court cartoon style

scenes.text: The courtiers filled their pumpkins with gold and jewels, thinking they were valuable.
scenes.image_prompt: courtiers putting gold and jewels inside pumpkins cartoon

scenes.summary: Tenali fills his pumpkin with curd.
scenes.text: Tenali made a small hole and filled his pumpkin with curd, then sealed it.
scenes.image_prompt: Tenali filling pumpkin with curd secretly cartoon

scenes.text: The king checked all pumpkins but was not impressed until he saw Tenali’s.
scenes.image_prompt: king inspecting pumpkins in court cartoon

scenes.text: Tenali explained that curd represents knowledge. The king praised him as the wisest.
scenes.image_prompt: Tenali explaining to king while others look surprised cartoon

story: The king asked his courtiers to fill a pumpkin with the wisest thing. Others chose gold and jewels, but Tenali filled his with curd, explaining it represents knowledge. The king declared him the wisest.
